# Overview of psychiatric emergencies

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Psychiatry > Basics of psychiatry > Overview of psychiatric emergencies*

[Original Article Link](/library/kH0mqh)

---

## Summary

This article gives an overview of the most common psychiatric emergencies and how to treat them.

---

## Overview

| Overview of psychiatric emergencies |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Condition | <u>Risk factors</u>/pathogenesis | Clinical features | Diagnostics | Management |
| <u>Suicidal behavior</u> | <br>* <u>Risk factors for suicidal behavior</u> include:<br><br>* Previous <u>suicide attempt</u> (most important <u>risk factor</u>)<br><br>* Psychiatric conditions<br><br>* <u>Schizophrenia</u><br><br>* <u>Psychosis</u><br><br>* <u>Mood disorders</u> (especially <u>major depressive disorder</u> and <u>bipolar disorder</u>)<br><br>* <u>Alcohol</u> or <u>substance use disorder</u><br><br>* <u>Eating disorders</u><br><br>* Social factors (e.g., unemployment, low <u>socioeconomic status</u>)<br><br>* Personal factors (male sex, possession of firearms)<br><br> | <br>* Clinical features of the underlying condition<br><br> | <br>* Psychiatric evaluation, involving the direct exploration of:<br><br>* <u>Suicidal ideation</u><br><br>* Concrete intent/plans<br><br>* Potential underlying conditions<br><br>* Previous <u>suicide attempts</u><br><br> | <br><br>* Acute management<br><br>* Imminent risk: hospitalization (if necessary, against the patient's will)<br><br>* Elevated risk <br><br>* Involvement of family<br><br>* Measures to increase patient's social contacts and interaction with medical professionals<br><br>* Long-term management<br><br>* Treatment of underlying psychiatric disorders (e.g., with <u>mood stabilizers</u>, <u>antidepressants</u>)<br><br>* Counseling: providing assistance in improving the patient's social circumstances, as well as development of problem-solving and coping skills<br><br><br> |
| <u>Neuroleptic malignant syndrome</u> | <br><br>* Central <u>D2 receptor</u> blockade in the <u>nigrostriatal pathway</u> and <u>hypothalamus</u> after intake of:<br><br>* <u>Antipsychotic drugs</u> (<u>high-potency FGAs</u> > <u>SGAs</u>)<br><br>* Agents that affect the <u>CNS</u> (e.g., <u>carbamazepine</u>, <u>lithium</u>)<br><br>* Certain <u>antiemetics</u> (e.g., <u>metoclopramide</u>, <u>promethazine</u>)<br><br>* Genetic predisposition<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Movement impairment: muscle rigidity (<u>lead-pipe rigidity</u>), <u>akinesia</u>, <u>tremor</u><br><br>* <u>Autonomic instability</u><br><br>* <u>Hyperthermia</u>, <u>diaphoresis</u><br><br>* Cardiovascular instability<br><br>* <u>Tachypnea</u><br><br>* <u>Altered mental status</u>: reduced vigilance, <u>stupor</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* ↑↑ <u>Creatine kinase</u><br><br>* <u>Leukocytosis</u><br><br>* <u>Metabolic acidosis</u><br><br>* <u>Myoglobinuria</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Discontinuation<br><br>* Pharmacotherapy<br><br>* <u>Dantrolene</u><br><br>* Alternatives: <u>bromocriptine</u>, <u>apomorphine</u>, or <u>amantadine</u><br><br>* <u>Benzodiazepines</u><br><br><br> |
| <u>Lithium toxicity</u> | <br>* Elevated <u>lithium</u> concentrations as a result of:<br><br>* Overdose (e.g., due to increased dosage)<br><br>* Renal impairment<br><br>* Low <u>effective circulating volume</u> (e.g., due to <u>dehydration</u>, <u>loop diuretic</u> use)<br><br>* Concomitant medication use that increases renal absorption of <u>lithium</u> (e.g., <u>NSAIDs</u>, <u>ACE inhibitors</u>)<br><br> | <br><br>* Gastrointestinal: <u>nausea</u>, <u>vomiting</u>, <u>diarrhea</u><br><br>* Neuromuscular<br><br>* <u>Ataxia</u>, slurred speech, <u>nystagmus</u><br><br>* <u>Fasciculations</u>, <u>hyperreflexia</u><br><br>* Coarse <u>tremors</u>, <u>seizures</u><br><br>* <u>Altered mental status</u>: <u>delirium</u>, confusion, <u>somnolence</u><br><br>* <u>Acute renal failure</u><br><br><br> | <br>* Blood work: <u>lithium</u> serum levels > 1.5 mEq/L<br><br> | <br><br>* Discontinuation<br><br>* Hydration with isotonic fluid<br><br>* Severe <u>lithium toxicity</u>: <u>hemodialysis</u>, ventilatory support if required<br><br><br> |
| <br>* <u>Clinical diagnosis</u>: <u>patient history</u> and clinical features<br><br> |  |  |  |  |
| <u>Malignant catatonia</u> | <br><br>* Associated with neuropsychiatric conditions, especially <u>schizophrenia</u><br><br>* Thought to be the result of <u>neurotransmitter</u> dysregulation<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Autonomic dysregulation<br><br>* <u>Fever</u>, sweating<br><br>* Cardiovascular instability, <u>tachypnea</u><br><br>* Movement impairment: rigidity<br><br>* <u>Altered mental status</u>: <u>delirium</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Discontinuation of <u>dopamine</u> blocking drugs<br><br>* <u>Benzodiazepines</u> (intravenous or sublingual <u>lorazepam</u>)<br><br>* <u>ECT</u><br><br><br> |  |
| <u>Serotonin syndrome</u> | <br><br>* Ingestion of <u>serotonergic agents</u> that increase the activity of <u>serotonin</u> <u>receptors</u>, including:<br><br>* Psychiatric drugs (e.g., <u>MAOIs</u>, <u>SSRIs</u>, <u>SNRIs</u>)<br><br>* Other drugs (e.g., <u>tramadol</u>, <u>ondansetron</u>, <u>linezolid</u>)<br><br>* Increased risk under the following conditions:<br><br>* Concurrent use of two or more <u>serotonergic drugs</u><br><br>* Switching from one <u>serotonergic drug</u> to another without tapering<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Neuromuscular excitability<br><br>* Hypertonia, <u>myoclonus</u><br><br>* <u>Hyperreflexia</u>, <u>tremor</u>, <u>seizure</u><br><br>* <u>Hyperthermia</u><br><br>* <u>Autonomic dysfunction</u><br><br>* <u>Diaphoresis</u>, <u>mydriasis</u><br><br>* Cardiovascular instability<br><br>* Gastrointestinal upset<br><br>* <u>Altered mental status</u>: <u>delirium</u>, <u>psychomotor agitation</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Discontinuation<br><br>* <u>Supportive care</u>: <u>cyproheptadine</u>, <u>antihypertensives</u>, <u>fluid replacement</u>, <u>benzodiazepines</u><br><br><br> |  |
| <u>Delirium tremens</u> | <br>* <u>Alcohol withdrawal</u> in individuals with chronic <u>alcohol</u> use<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Altered mental status</u><br><br>* Visual and <u>tactile hallucinations</u><br><br>* Impaired consciousness and <u>disorientation</u>, <u>anxiety</u>, <u>disorganized thinking</u><br><br>* Increased suggestibility<br><br>* <u>Psychomotor agitation</u><br><br>* Fidgeting, restlessness, emotional lability<br><br>* Reversal of the <u>sleep</u>-wake cycle<br><br>* <u>Insomnia</u><br><br>* <u>Autonomic instability</u>: <u>tachycardia</u>, <u>hypertension</u>, <u>nausea</u><br><br>* Additional symptoms in <u>delirium tremens</u>:<br><br>* <u>Alcohol withdrawal seizures</u><br><br>* Rest and <u>intention tremor</u> (first high frequency, then low frequency)<br><br><br> | <br><br>* First-line: <u>benzodiazepines</u><br><br>* Shorter or intermediate-acting (e.g., <u>oxazepam</u>, <u>lorazepam</u>): Consider in patients with a slow metabolism (e.g., the elderly, those with <u>liver</u> failure)<br><br>* Longer acting (e.g., <u>chlordiazepoxide</u>, <u>diazepam</u>): preferred in all other patients<br><br>* Second-line: <u>anticonvulsants</u> (in case of <u>contraindications for benzodiazepines</u>)<br><br><br> |  |
| <u>Delirium</u> | <br><br>* Pediatric, elderly (> 65 years), and hospitalized patients are particularly susceptible<br><br>* Most commonly associated with metabolic conditions, such as <u>electrolyte</u> abnormalities, <u>thyroid</u> disturbances<br><br>* Other precipitating factors include:<br><br>* Infections (most commonly <u>UTIs</u>, <u>pneumonia</u>)<br><br>* Trauma, <u>CNS</u> pathologies, <u>hypoxia</u>, acute cardiovascular disease<br><br>* Drugs and toxins (e.g., <u>anticholinergics</u>, sedatives, <u>opioids</u>)<br><br>* <u>Alcohol</u> and illicit substance intoxication/withdrawal<br><br>* Ongoing symptoms (e.g., <u>dehydration</u>, <u>urinary retention</u>)<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Treatment of the underlying condition (e.g., discontinuation of precipitating medication, <u>antibiotic</u> treatment of infection)<br><br>* Maintain adequate hydration<br><br>* Reduce confusion (e.g., reorientation to time, place, and person)<br><br><br> |  |  |
| <u>Acute dystonia</u> | <br>* Inhibition of <u>nigrostriatal</u> <u>dopaminergic pathways</u> caused by <u>antagonism</u> at <u>D2 receptors</u> after <u>antipsychotic</u> intake<br><br> | <br>* Movement impairment<br><br>* Painful and lasting muscle spasms and stiffness<br><br>* <u>Torticollis</u><br><br>* <u>Oculogyric crisis</u><br><br>* In severe cases: <u>laryngospasm</u><br><br> | <br><br>* First-line: <u>benztropine</u><br><br>* Alternatives: <u>diphenhydramine</u>, <u>benzodiazepines</u><br><br>* In case of <u>laryngospasm</u>: <u>intubation</u><br><br><br> |  |
| <u>Tyramine</u>-induced <u>hypertensive crisis</u> | <br><br>* Ingestion of <u>tyramine</u>-rich foods, including aged smoked/cured meats and alcoholic beverages (especially beer and red wine)<br><br>* <u>Tyramine</u> stimulates the <u>sympathetic nervous system</u> by releasing other <u>neurotransmitters</u>, such as <u>noradrenaline</u>, from <u>vesicles</u> into the <u>synaptic cleft</u>.<br><br><br> | <br>* <u>Hypertensive crisis</u> (see “<u>Clinical features of hypertensive crises</u>” for details)<br><br> | <br><br>* Usually <u>self-limiting</u>, depending on the amount of ingested <u>tyramine</u><br><br>* Rapid blood pressure reduction is contraindicated<br><br><br> |  |
| <u>Tricyclic antidepressant toxicity</u> | <br>* Ingestion of <u>tricyclic antidepressants</u> which cause various effects, including:<br><br>* <u>Muscarinic ACh receptor</u> inhibition<br><br>* Cardiac fast <u>sodium</u> channel inhibition<br><br>* GABA<sub>A</sub> inhibition<br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Anticholinergic effects</u><br><br>* <u>Hyperpyrexia</u>, flushed and dry <u>skin</u>, thirst, <u>mydriasis</u><br><br>* See “<u>Anticholinergic syndrome</u>.”<br><br>* Cardiotoxic effects: prolonged <u>QTc</u>, <u>arrhythmias</u><br><br>* <u>Neurotoxicity</u>: <u>seizures</u>, <u>coma</u>, respiratory <u>depression</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Supportive treatment, e.g., securing <u>airways</u>, oxygenation<br><br>* <u>Activated charcoal</u><br><br>* <u>Sodium bicarbonate</u> for treatment and prevention of <u>cardiac arrhythmia</u>: monitor with <u>ECG</u><br><br><br> |  |
| <br>* <u>ECG</u>: prolonged <u>QTc</u> and QRS<br><br> |  |  |  |  |
